row1.text: Work, approvals and connections: Home as my work, the merge checklist, the confirm-class card, and where each tool comes from

row2.text: Evidence, restarts and checks: the audit log, what a restart shows, the latency readout, and checks on any branch

n1.text: Every control shown exists in the plan: cards are named by the Jira or GitLab query that fills them, and each write names the exact remote effect before the button.

n2.text: Merge stays disabled until every precondition read live from GitLab is green. GitLab enforces the same rules server-side, so a stale view fails, never merges wrong.

n3.text: Confirm class: jira_transition, jira_log_time, gitlab_create_mr, gitlab_merge. Only Allow once and Reject. Reads ran without a card, shown as plain rows.

n4.text: Each row has an intent and a result; the remote id joins it to Jira's issue history or GitLab's MR activity, which stay the evidence of record.

n5.text: Desktop only: a reboot ends every process. Home lists intents without results and flows that stopped mid-way; the chat marks the interrupted turn. Nothing is replayed silently.

n6.text: The readout is the budget table of plan §1, per turn, from the CLI's OpenTelemetry export to a local file. Record Performance Trace turns it on for one restart.

n7.text: Jira and GitLab are the team's own MCP containers from .gemini/settings.json. Measured: 48 + 58 tools, about 29,000 tokens of schemas on every request. The adapter takes them over, keeps the tokens in the keychain, and re-exposes 17 tools (about 1,600 tokens).

n8.text: Pick any branch; a branch not checked out gets its own reusable checkout. Snyk runs locally; SonarQube's gate needs one push until local analysis through the official MCP server lands. Fix starts an agent on the branch.
